historical_transitions.summary: Frankencoin (ZCHF) core deployed at block 18451518 (receipt contractAddress 0xB58E61C3098d85632Df34EecfB899A1Ed80921cB, 7626-byte runtime at the deployment block); its constructor internally creates the Frankencoin Pool Shares (FPS) equity contract 0x1bA26788dfDe592fec8bcB0Eaff472a42BE341B2 (verified: 8627-byte runtime, name 'Frankencoin Pool Share', symbol FPS), establishing the original share-governance control plane with the legacy >= 2% FPS holder veto.

Frankencoin Shares (FCS) deployed at block 25852506 as a non-proxy ERC-4626-style share contract whose underlying asset is the ZCHF core (asset() returns 0xB58E61C3098d85632Df34EecfB899A1Ed80921cB). The first Wrapped event executes 25 minutes later at block 25852635, beginning the migration of the share-governance narrative from legacy FPS to FCS while the ZCHF core remains untouched.

83 days post-deployment the FCS runtime bytecode at block 26450479 is byte-identical to the deployment-block output (both probes return 22902 hex chars, sha256 prefix c6b63573a29d8d8b): no proxy upgrade and no admin controller. The block carries an ordinary FCS transaction (tx 0xe1c8f2d2...), so usage continues under unchanged code.

evidence_sources.claim_summary: Pre-migration documentation presents Frankencoin Pool Shares (FPS) as the protocol's equity and governance token (26 FPS mentions) with zero FCS mentions across the crawled docs.frankencoin.com pages (Wayback capture 2026-07-12).

Commit 'docs: add audited FCS mechanics and migration reference' (2fe13b59aa) is the FIRST commit in fcs.md's history - the file did not exist before 2026-09-18T08:35:11Z. It adds fcs.md, fcs-migration.md and governance.md, making FCS the canonical share narrative and closing the post-launch documentation gap.
Post-repair snapshot: the docs index now references FCS / Frankencoin Shares extensively (53 mentions), confirming the migration documentation was publicly live by 2026-10-09.

Commit a1322816a2 (2026-09-28) rewrote governance.md, fcs.md and fps-reference.md to document a single shared 1% quorum (Governance.sol QUORUM = 100 bps) for both FCS-based and legacy FPS actions, stating legacy FPS is 'no longer 2%'. The immutable deployed 2023 Equity (FPS) contract 0x1bA26788dfDe592fec8bcB0Eaff472a42BE341B2 carries QUORUM = 200 bps in its verified source (Sourcify), so FPS1 still enforces a 2% veto on-chain while the docs describe a unified 1%.

gap_windows.summary: FCS governance wrapper live on-chain at block 25852506 (2026-08-28) while docs.frankencoin.com still documented only FPS (Wayback 2026-07-12). The gitbook repo's continuous commit history binds the gap end-to-end: zero commits exist between 2026-08-28T00:00:00Z and 2026-09-18T08:29:18Z, and fcs.md's own file history begins with commit 2fe13b59aa at 2026-09-18T08:35:11Z (block 26003224), so within the inspected surfaces - the 2026-07-12 Wayback capture of docs.frankencoin.com and the gitbook repository's commit history - no FCS documentation existed in the window. MTTR = 21 days.

Aligned FCS interval: documented FCS mechanics (non-proxy ERC-4626-style wrapper; underlying ZCHF via asset() = 0xB58E61C3098d85632Df34EecfB899A1Ed80921cB; > 1% FCS quorum per shipped Governance.sol QUORUM = 100) match on-chain reality across blocks 26003224-26450479 (bytecode identical at both endpoints). eth_getLogs census on 0xDb861830D9Ae2d1fCF99fA0cfd3973de382B0B5b (fromBlock 25852506/0x18a7a5a, toBlock 26450479/0x1939a2f, dual-provider): 50 Wrapped and 34 Deposit events (topics 0x4700c172... / 0xdcbc1c05...). Governance route live: ZCHF emitted MinterDenied at block 26315046.

Adverse legacy-FPS divergence, introduced by docs commit a1322816a2 (Frankencoin-ZCHF/gitbook, 2026-09-28T11:54:19Z; first block at/after commit = 26075784): docs now describe legacy FPS as sharing the same unified 1% quorum ('no longer 2%'), while the immutable 2023 FPS contract (QUORUM = 200, verified source) still enforces a 2% veto. Window remains open at the 2026-11-19 checkpoint (block 26450479; 52 calendar days elapsed from 2026-09-28 to 2026-11-19): the contradiction is unresolved in docs and contracts as of that date.

executive_risk_memo: Frankencoin runs an oracle-free Swiss-franc CDP whose share-governance control plane migrated in August 2026: Frankencoin Shares (FCS, 0xDb861830D9Ae2d1fCF99fA0cfd3973de382B0B5b) is a non-proxy ERC-4626-style share contract whose underlying asset is the ZCHF core itself (asset() = 0xB58E61C3098d85632Df34EecfB899A1Ed80921cB, deployed 2023-10-28 at block 18451518), while the legacy equity contract FPS (0x1bA26788dfDe592fec8bcB0Eaff472a42BE341B2) remains on-chain. FCS is byte-identical between deployment block 25852506 and checkpoint block 26450479 (sha256 prefix c6b63573a29d8d8b), so no admin key can mutate the share ledger. Governance power rests on a > 1% FCS binding-vote route - distinct from the legacy 2% FPS veto, which the immutable 2023 FPS contract still enforces even though the docs now describe a unified 1% quorum - and it is not theoretical: the ZCHF core emitted MinterDenied at block 26315046 (tx 0xafeb41ec...), the first exercised denial of the FCS era, alongside 50 Wrapped and 34 Deposit events over the deployment-to-checkpoint window (dual-provider eth_getLogs census). Documentation lagged deployment by 21 days (MTTR = 21): fcs.md first appears in gitbook commit 2fe13b59aa on 2026-09-18, three weeks after the on-chain launch, leaving integrators to read source during the gap. The legacy-FPS divergence is a separate, still-open finding (introduced by docs commit a1322816a2 on 2026-09-28; 52 days open at the 2026-11-19 checkpoint), so the dossier reports partially_repaired overall. Engineering concentration is the dominant residual risk: 152 commits in 12 months (96 contract-touching) but only 4 human contributors with a bus factor of 2 (Luzius Meisser and samclassix author 96 percent). With roughly $52.9M protocol-wide Frankencoin (ZCHF) TVL per DefiLlama (pacta slug frankencoin) - not standalone assets locked inside the FCS governance wrapper - the posture is technically sound yet operationally fragile: monitor binding-vote participation, FPS-to-FCS residue, and documentation freshness rather than upgradeability.
